description: The European Cooperation for Space Standardization (ECSS) publishes a coherent single set of standards, handbooks and technical memoranda for all European space activities. Two engineering standards matter most for space weather and infrastructure resilience: ECSS-E-ST-10-04C Rev.1 Space environment (15 June 2020), which defines the natural environment for all space regimes and general models and rules for determining the local induced environment, and ECSS-E-ST-20-06C Rev.1 Spacecraft charging (15 May 2019), which sets provisions for assessing and avoiding charging effects on any spacecraft, including launchers above the atmosphere. The website also offers a long list of published standards, document requirement definitions, an applicability requirement matrix, a glossary and historical ESA PSS specifications. Standards are maintained by the ECSS Secretariat at ESA-ESTEC in Noordwijk and published as PDF and Word files. The site asks users to register before use, and ESA holds copyright for all ECSS documents: reproduction needs ESA's consent, which is granted to ECSS members for their own use and their contractors; no fee is mentioned on the pages read. Caveats: the standards are normative texts, not data, and use outside ECSS members needs ESA consent. They support hazard exposure and resilience assumptions for satellite design and space weather modelling; a related record is the US Space Industry Technical Standards Compendium.
